questions.prompt: Do you like meeting people from other countries?
questions.sampleA1: Yes, I like. I like meeting new people. They are nice.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like meeting people. They are from other countries. It is interesting because they are different.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I like meeting people from other countries. It is very interesting to learn about their culture. For example, I met someone from Japan, and they told me about the tea ceremony. However, sometimes it is difficult to understand their English. But I still like it.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I love it. Meeting people from other countries is one of my favourite things, because you get a real taste of how differently people actually live. I suppose it also broadens your horizons — you pick up little bits of their language, and, more often than not, you hit it off almost straight away.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha, menga yoqadi. Men yangi odamlar bilan tanishishni yoqtiraman. Ular yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men odamlar bilan tanishishni yoqtiraman. Ular boshqa davlatlardan. Bu qiziq, chunki ular boshqacha.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, menga boshqa davlatlardan kelgan odamlar bilan tanishish yoqadi. Ularning madaniyati haqida bilish juda qiziqarli.
Masalan, men Yaponiyalik bir odam bilan tanishdim va u menga choy marosimi haqida gapirib berdi.
Lekin, ba'zida ularning ingliz tilini tushunish qiyin bo'ladi. Lekin menga baribir yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men albatta boshqa davlatlardan kelgan odamlar bilan tanishishdan zavqlanaman. Bu turli madaniyatlar va nuqtai nazarlar haqida o'rganish uchun ajoyib imkoniyat. Aslida, yaqinda men Argentinadan kelgan bir odam bilan tanishdim va biz siyosiy tizimlarimiz o'rtasidagi farqlar haqida juda qiziqarli suhbatlashdik. Bu haqiqatan ham ko'zingizni ochadi. Garchi ba'zida til to'siqlari tufayli muloqot biroz qiyin bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, odatda buni yengib o'tish mumkin.

idioms: get along like a house on fire - "qalin do'st bo'lib ketmoq"

"Meeting new people is..." - "Yangi odamlar bilan uchrashish bu..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Absolutely, I derive immense pleasure from meeting individuals from diverse cultural backgrounds. It's an enriching experience that broadens my perspective and challenges my preconceived notions. Frankly, I believe that engaging with people from different countries is crucial for fostering global understanding and empathy.

These interactions often lead to stimulating conversations about history, traditions, and ways of life. I find it fascinating to learn about customs that starkly contrast with my own, and I make a conscious effort to understand the underlying reasons for these differences. Moreover, it's a fantastic way to improve my language skills and even pick up a few phrases in other languages. It’s a win-win, as they say. When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Albatta, men turli madaniyatlarga mansub odamlar bilan tanishishdan juda katta zavq olaman. Bu mening dunyoqarashimni kengaytiradigan va oldindan shakllangan tushunchalarimga qarshi chiqadigan boyituvchi tajriba. Ochig'ini aytsam, boshqa davlatlardan kelgan odamlar bilan muloqot qilish global tushunish va hamdardlikni rivojlantirish uchun juda muhim, deb hisoblayman.

Bu kabi muloqotlar ko'pincha tarix, urf-odatlar va turmush tarzi haqida qiziqarli suhbatlarga olib keladi. O'zimnikidan keskin farq qiladigan urf-odatlarni o'rganish men uchun juda qiziq va men bu farqlarning asosiy sabablarini tushunishga ongli ravishda harakat qilaman. Bundan tashqari, bu mening til ko'nikmalarimni yaxshilash va hatto boshqa tillarda bir nechta iboralarni o'rganishning ajoyib usuli. Aytishlaricha, bu ikki tomon uchun ham foydali. Qayerga borsang, shuning odatini qil.

questions.prompt: Do you enjoy listening to the radio?
questions.sampleA1: No, I don't. I don't like radio. Music is better.
questions.sampleA2: I don't listen to the radio often. I like music, and I have music on my phone. So I don't need the radio.
questions.sampleB1: I don't listen to the radio very much. I prefer to listen to music on my phone. For example, I can choose exactly what I want to listen to. However, sometimes the radio has good news.
questions.sampleB2: I do, actually, though maybe not as much as I used to. The thing is, I usually have it on in the background while I'm cooking or driving — it sort of keeps me company. I'm quite fond of the morning talk shows, to be honest, and I love how you stumble upon songs you'd never have chosen yourself.
questions.uzSampleA1: Yo'q, menga yoqmaydi. Men radioga yoqtirmayman. Musiqa yaxshiroq.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men radioga unchalik ko'p quloq solmayman. Menga musiqa yoqadi va telefonimda musiqam bor. Shuning uchun menga radio kerak emas.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men radioga unchalik ko'p quloq solmayman. Men telefonimda musiqa tinglashni afzal ko'raman.
Masalan, men aynan nimani tinglashni xohlasam, tanlashim mumkin.
Biroq, ba'zida radioda yaxshi yangiliklar bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Men hozirgi kunda radioga kamdan-kam quloq solaman. Men ko'proq striming xizmatlari yoki podkastlarni afzal ko'raman, chunki ular men eshitadigan narsalar ustidan ko'proq xilma-xillik va nazoratni taklif qiladi.
Shunga qaramay, men radioning mahalliy yangiliklar va favqulodda vaziyatlar haqidagi eshittirishlar uchun muhim maqsadga xizmat qilishini tan olaman.
Ba'zida, agar men ilgari eshitmagan narsaga kayfiyatim bo'lsa, mashinada radioga quloq solishim mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Do you...
idioms: to each their own - "har kimning o'z didi bor"
sentenceStarters: "I prefer listening to..." - "Men ...ni tinglashni afzal ko'raman"
"The radio is a good way to..." - "Radio ...ning yaxshi usuli"

questions.sampleAnswer:
To be honest, I don't really tune in to the radio very often these days. With the advent of streaming services and podcasts, the radio has become somewhat obsolete for me. That being said, I do appreciate the role it plays in providing local news and emergency broadcasts.

Occasionally, when I'm driving long distances, I might scan through the stations to see if there's anything interesting on. There's a certain nostalgia associated with listening to the radio, especially if they are playing old favourites. Ultimately, times have changed and I gravitate towards other forms of media that better suit my needs and preferences. It's a matter of personal taste, to each their own.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, men hozirgi kunda radioga unchalik ko'p quloq solmayman. Oqimli xizmatlar va podkastlar paydo bo'lishi bilan radio men uchun biroz eskirgan narsaga aylandi. Shunga qaramay, uning mahalliy yangiliklar va favqulodda vaziyatlar haqidagi xabarlarni yetkazishdagi rolini qadrlayman.

Ba'zan, uzoq masofalarga mashina haydab ketayotganimda, stansiyalarni ko'zdan kechirib, qiziqarli biror narsa bormi, yo'qmi, shuni bilmoqchi bo'laman. Radioga quloq solish bilan bog'liq ma'lum bir nostalji bor, ayniqsa ular eski sevimli qo'shiqlarni qo'yishsa. Oxir oqibat, zamon o'zgardi va men o'zimning ehtiyojlarim va xohishlarimga ko'proq mos keladigan boshqa media shakllariga moyil bo'lib qoldim. Bu shaxsiy did masalasi, har kimning o'ziga yarasha.

questions.prompt: Do you like going for walks?
questions.sampleA1: Yes, I like. I like walking. It is good.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like to walk. I walk in the park. It is nice and I like the trees.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I like going for walks. It's good exercise and I enjoy being outside. For example, I often walk in the park near my house. However, sometimes it's too cold or rainy to walk outside.
questions.sampleB2: Definitely — I'd say it's one of the best ways to wind down. Whenever I've had a hectic day, I head out for half an hour just to clear my head. The thing is, it doesn't really feel like exercise at all, and yet you come back feeling refreshed and recharged. Honestly, I can't get enough of it.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha, menga yoqadi. Men piyoda yurishni yoqtiraman. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men piyoda yurishni yaxshi ko'raman. Men parkda yuraman. U yer yoqimli va menga daraxtlar yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men piyoda yurishni yaxshi ko'raman. Bu yaxshi mashq va menga tashqarida bo'lish yoqadi.
Masalan, men ko'pincha uyimning yaqinidagi parkda piyoda yuraman.
Biroq, ba'zan tashqarida piyoda yurish uchun juda sovuq yoki yomg'irli bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men albatta sayr qilishni yoqtiraman. Bu mashq qilish va fikrlarimni tozalashning ajoyib usuli. Aslida, men haftada kamida bir necha marta sayr qilishga harakat qilaman. Bu menga uzoq kundan keyin dam olish va stressdan xalos bo'lishga yordam beradi. Bundan tashqari, bu mening mahalliy hududimni o'rganish uchun yaxshi imkoniyat.

vocabulary.title: Do you...
idioms: get a new lease on life - "yangi hayot boshlamoq"
sentenceStarters: "Walking is a great way to..." - "Piyoda yurish ...ning ajoyib usuli"
"I find walking very..." - "Men piyoda yurishni juda ... deb bilaman"
"I like to walk because..." - "Men piyoda yurishni yaxshi ko'raman, chunki..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'm quite fond of going for walks, yes. I find it to be an excellent way to de-stress and clear my head. The simple act of putting one foot in front of the other, coupled with fresh air and natural surroundings, can be incredibly therapeutic.

I particularly enjoy walking in parks or nature reserves where I can immerse myself in the beauty of the environment. It allows me to appreciate the small details that I might otherwise overlook in my busy daily life. Besides, it's a great way to get some exercise without putting too much strain on my body. In short, a good walk is just what the doctor ordered when I'm feeling overwhelmed or stressed. It helps you blow off steam.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men sayr qilishni juda yaxshi ko'raman, ha. Bu stressdan xalos bo'lish va fikrlarimni tartibga solishning ajoyib usuli deb bilaman. Bir oyoqni ikkinchisining oldiga qo'yishning oddiy harakati, toza havo va tabiiy muhit bilan birgalikda juda terapevtik bo'lishi mumkin.

Men ayniqsa bog'larda yoki tabiat qo'riqxonalarida sayr qilishni yoqtiraman, u yerda atrof-muhitning go'zalligiga sho'ng'ib ketishim mumkin. Bu menga band bo'lgan kundalik hayotimda e'tibordan chetda qoldirishim mumkin bo'lgan kichik detallarni qadrlashga imkon beradi. Bundan tashqari, bu tanamga juda ko'p zo'riqish bermasdan mashq qilishning ajoyib usuli. Qisqasi, yaxshi sayr - o'zimni haddan tashqari bosim ostida yoki stressda his qilganimda, aynan shifokor buyurgan narsa. Bu sizga dam olishga yordam beradi.

questions.prompt: Compare the pace of life depicted in these two images.
questions.sampleA1: The first picture is busy. The second picture is quiet. I like the quiet picture.
questions.sampleA2: The first picture is a city, and it is very busy. The second picture is a garden, and it is quiet. I like the garden because it is peaceful.
questions.sampleB1: The first picture shows a busy city with lots of traffic. The second picture shows a quiet garden. For example, in the city people are rushing. However, in the garden, someone is reading a book and relaxing. I prefer the garden.
questions.sampleB2: Well, these two couldn't be more different. The first one shows a bustling city — probably somewhere like Times Square — with yellow taxis, a red double-decker bus, giant flashing billboards and crowds rushing about everywhere. It's the rat race in a nutshell. The second, by contrast, is a sleepy stone village where an elderly man is walking his little dog down a winding lane, surrounded by rolling green hills. The pace there is slow and unhurried, whereas the city is go, go, go. Personally, I'd plump for the village any day.
questions.uzSampleA1: Birinchi rasm gavjum. Ikkinchi rasm tinch. Menga tinch rasm yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Birinchi rasm - shahar, va u juda gavjum. Ikkinchi rasm - bog', va u tinch. Menga bog' yoqadi, chunki u osoyishta.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Birinchi rasmda tirbandlik ko'p bo'lgan gavjum shahar ko'rsatilgan. Ikkinchi rasmda esa sokin bog' tasvirlangan.
Masalan, shaharda odamlar shoshilishmoqda.
Biroq, bog'da kimdir kitob o'qib, dam olmoqda. Menga bog' ko'proq yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Birinchi rasmda tez sur'atli shahar hayoti, osmono'par binolar va tirbandlik aks etgan bo'lib, bu gavjum va stressli muhitni ko'rsatadi.
Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda bog'da kitob o'qiyotgan odamning tinch manzarasi tasvirlangan bo'lib, bu sekinroq va xotirjam sur'atni ifodalaydi. Shahar rasmi ambitsiya va doimiy faollikni nazarda tutsa, bog' rasmi xotirjamlik va qoniqishni taklif qiladi. Asosan, biri qilish haqida, ikkinchisi esa bo'lish haqida, bu xuddi olma bilan apelsinni solishtirishga o'xshaydi.

vocabulary.title: Compare the...
sentenceStarters: "The first image shows..." - "Birinchi rasmda ... ko'rsatilgan"
"In contrast, the second image..." - "Aksincha, ikkinchi rasm..."
"The main difference is..." - "Asosiy farq shundaki..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
The contrast between the pace of life depicted in these two images is quite striking. The first image portrays a fast-paced urban environment, characterized by towering skyscrapers, congested streets, and people hurrying about their business. It evokes a sense of urgency and constant motion, where time seems to be of the essence. Conversely, the second image offers a starkly different scene, showcasing a tranquil rural setting with a person leisurely reading in a garden or a serene nature scene in a quiet village.

The city scene represents the pressures and demands of modern life, where individuals are constantly juggling multiple responsibilities and striving to meet deadlines. It's a world of ambition, competition, and relentless pursuit of success. On the other hand, the rural scene embodies a slower, more deliberate pace of life, where individuals prioritize relaxation, contemplation, and connection with nature. It's a world of simplicity, tranquility, and appreciation for the present moment. Ultimately, both lifestyles have their own merits and drawbacks, and the ideal pace of life is subjective and dependent on individual preferences. It boils down to what you value most.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki suratda tasvirlangan hayot tarzi o'rtasidagi farq juda sezilarli. Birinchi suratda tez sur'atli shahar muhiti tasvirlangan bo'lib, unda baland osmono'par binolar, tirband ko'chalar va o'z ishlari bilan shoshayotgan odamlar aks etgan. Bu shoshilinchlik va doimiy harakat hissini uyg'otadi, go'yo vaqt juda qadrlidek. Aksincha, ikkinchi surat butunlay boshqacha manzarani taqdim etadi, unda bog'da bemalol kitob o'qiyotgan odam yoki tinch qishloqdagi sokin tabiat manzarasi aks etgan.

Shahar manzarasi zamonaviy hayotning bosimi va talablarini aks ettiradi, bunda odamlar doimiy ravishda bir nechta vazifalarni bajarishga harakat qilishadi va belgilangan muddatlarga rioya qilishga intilishadi. Bu ambitsiya, raqobat va muvaffaqiyatga tinimsiz intilish dunyosi. Boshqa tomondan, qishloq manzarasi hayotning sekinroq va o'ylangan tarzini o'zida mujassam etgan bo'lib, unda odamlar dam olish, tafakkur va tabiat bilan aloqaga ustunlik berishadi. Bu soddalik, xotirjamlik va hozirgi lahzani qadrlash dunyosi. Oxir oqibat, har ikki turmush tarzining o'z afzalliklari va kamchiliklari bor va hayotning ideal sur'ati sub'ektiv va individual xohishlarga bog'liq. Bu siz eng ko'p nimani qadrlashingizga bog'liq.

questions.prompt: How does spending time in nature improve a person's mental clarity and productivity?
questions.sampleA1: Nature is good. It makes you happy. You can walk there.
questions.sampleA2: Nature is quiet and nice. City is loud. I like nature because it is relaxing.
questions.sampleB1: Nature is very calming. It helps you think better. For example, you can go to a park. However, the city is very noisy. It can make you stressed. Nature helps with your mental health.
questions.sampleB2: To my mind, nature works wonders. When you're surrounded by greenery, all that mental clutter just melts away, and you can finally think straight. I suppose stepping away from your screens gives your brain a chance to recharge, so once you're back at your desk you're far sharper and you get more done. It genuinely clears the mind.
questions.uzSampleA1: Tabiat yaxshi. U sizni xursand qiladi. U yerda piyoda yurishingiz mumkin.
questions.uzSampleA2: Tabiat sokin va yoqimli. Shahar shovqinli. Menga tabiat yoqadi, chunki u dam beradi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Tabiat juda tinchlantiruvchi. U yaxshiroq o'ylashingizga yordam beradi.
Masalan, siz bog'ga borishingiz mumkin.
Biroq, shahar juda shovqinli. U sizni stressga solishi mumkin. Tabiat sizning ruhiy salomatligingizga yordam beradi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Tabiatda vaqt o'tkazish sizning ruhiy holatingizni sezilarli darajada yaxshilashi mumkin. Tinchlik va osoyishtalik sizga dam olishga va fikrlaringizni tozalashga yordam beradi.
Bundan tashqari, ochiq havoda bo'lish ko'pincha jismoniy faollikni rag'batlantiradi, bu ham miyangiz uchun foydali. Bu ikki tomonlama foyda.
Biroq, ko'p odamlar shahar hayotining talablaridan qochishni qiyin deb bilishadi.

vocabulary.title: How does spending...
sentenceStarters: "Spending time in nature..." - "Tabiatda vaqt o'tkazish..."
"Nature can improve..." - "Tabiat yaxshilashi mumkin..."
"Being outdoors helps..." - "Ochiq havoda bo'lish yordam beradi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Spending time in nature offers a trifecta of benefits for mental clarity and productivity. Firstly, the reduction in sensory overload is crucial. Urban environments bombard us with constant noise and visual stimuli, which inevitably leads to mental fatigue. Nature, on the other hand, provides a calming, predictable environment, allowing our brains to rest and recharge.

Secondly, exposure to natural light and fresh air stimulates the production of serotonin and vitamin D, both of which are essential for mood regulation and cognitive function. It's like hitting the reset button on your brain. Studies have shown a direct correlation between time spent outdoors and improved concentration levels. Furthermore, the physical activity often associated with being in nature, such as hiking or even a simple walk in the park, increases blood flow to the brain, further enhancing cognitive performance. A sound mind in a sound body, as they say.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Tabiatda vaqt o'tkazish ruhiy tiniqlik va unumdorlik uchun uch karra foyda beradi. Birinchidan, sezgi ortiqchaligining kamayishi juda muhim. Shahar muhitlari bizni doimiy shovqin va vizual stimullar bilan bombardimon qiladi, bu esa muqarrar ravishda ruhiy charchoqqa olib keladi. Tabiat esa, aksincha, tinchlantiruvchi, bashorat qilinadigan muhitni ta'minlaydi, bu bizning miyalarimizga dam olish va qayta zaryadlash imkonini beradi.

Ikkinchidan, tabiiy yorug'lik va toza havoga ta'sir qilish serotonin va D vitaminining ishlab chiqarilishini rag'batlantiradi, ularning ikkalasi ham kayfiyatni tartibga solish va kognitiv funktsiya uchun zarurdir. Bu miyangizni qayta yuklash tugmachasini bosish bilan bir xil. Tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatdiki, ochiq havoda o'tkazilgan vaqt va diqqatni jamlash darajasining yaxshilanishi o'rtasida bevosita bog'liqlik mavjud. Bundan tashqari, tabiatda bo'lish bilan bog'liq bo'lgan jismoniy faollik, masalan, piyoda yurish yoki hatto parkda oddiygina sayr qilish, miyaga qon oqimini oshiradi, bu esa kognitiv ishlashni yanada yaxshilaydi. Sog'lom tanada sog'lom aql bo'ladi, deyishadi.

questions.prompt: Why is it becoming increasingly difficult for people to completely disconnect from city life?
questions.sampleA1: City is busy. Internet is there. People work in city.
questions.sampleA2: City is good for work. But city is loud. It is hard to relax because of the noise.
questions.sampleB1: It is hard to disconnect from the city. People need jobs there. For example, many companies are in the city. However, the city is very connected. It is hard to escape technology.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the honest truth is we're glued to our screens these days. With work emails and social media following you around, it's almost impossible to switch off. On top of that, most decent jobs are based in the city, so people feel tied down financially. I suppose the noise and the buzz become second nature, and stepping away feels harder than it really should.
questions.uzSampleA1: Shahar gavjum. Internet bor. Odamlar shaharda ishlaydi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Shahar ish uchun yaxshi. Lekin shahar shovqinli. Shovqin tufayli dam olish qiyin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Shahardan uzilish qiyin. Odamlarga u yerda ish kerak.
Misol uchun, ko'plab kompaniyalar shaharda joylashgan.
Biroq, shahar juda bog'langan. Texnologiyadan qochish qiyin.
questions.uzSampleB2: Shahar hayotidan uzilish tobora qiyinlashib bormoqda. Texnologiya o'chirishni qiyinlashtiradi. Shuningdek, ko'p odamlar ish imkoniyatlari uchun shaharlarda yashashlari kerak. Ish va dam olish o'rtasida muvozanatni topish qiyin. Doimiy aloqa haddan tashqari bo'lishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Why is it...
sentenceStarters: "It is becoming difficult..." - "Qiyinlashib bormoqda..."
"People are connected to..." - "Odamlar bilan bog'langan..."
"Technology makes it hard to..." - "Texnologiya qiyinlashtiradi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
It's undeniably becoming increasingly difficult to completely disconnect from city life due to several converging factors. Firstly, technology plays a significant role. The ubiquitous nature of smartphones and the internet means that we are constantly connected to work, social media, and news cycles. It's hard to switch off when your email is always accessible.

Secondly, the economic pressures of modern life often necessitate being close to urban centers where job opportunities are concentrated. Many people simply can't afford to live in more remote, rural areas. Finally, the convenience and amenities offered by city life, such as easy access to shopping, entertainment, and healthcare, are difficult to give up. Old habits die hard, and the conveniences of urban living have become deeply ingrained in our daily routines.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Shubhasiz, bir qancha omillar tufayli shahar hayotidan butunlay uzilish tobora qiyinlashib bormoqda. Birinchidan, texnologiya muhim rol o'ynaydi. Smartfonlar va internetning keng tarqalganligi biz doimo ish, ijtimoiy tarmoqlar va yangiliklar bilan bog'langanimizni anglatadi. Elektron pochtangiz doimo mavjud bo'lsa, o'chirish qiyin.

Ikkinchidan, zamonaviy hayotning iqtisodiy bosimi ko'pincha ish imkoniyatlari to'plangan shahar markazlariga yaqin bo'lishni talab qiladi. Ko'p odamlar shunchaki uzoqroq, qishloq joylarda yashashga qurbi yetmaydi. Nihoyat, shahar hayoti taqdim etadigan qulayliklar va imkoniyatlar, masalan, xarid qilish, ko'ngilochar va sog'liqni saqlash xizmatlariga oson kirishdan voz kechish qiyin. Eski odatlar o'lmaydi va shahar hayotining qulayliklari kundalik hayotimizga chuqur singib ketgan.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you taught someone a practical skill.
questions.sampleA1: I taught my brother. He learned to ride a bike. It was fun.
questions.sampleA2: I taught my sister to cook. It was hard, but she learned. Now she can cook pasta.
questions.sampleB1: I taught my friend how to play guitar. It was difficult at first. For example, he couldn't hold the chords. However, he practiced a lot. Now he can play some songs. Informal learning is important.
questions.sampleB2: Right, so the skill that springs to mind is cooking — a couple of years ago I taught my younger sister how to make a proper homemade pilaf, which is a bit of a family staple where I'm from. To be honest, she could barely boil an egg at the time, so we started from scratch. I walked her through the whole thing step by step — how to chop up the carrots, when to add the rice, how to judge the heat. At first she was all fingers and thumbs and nearly gave up, but I kept reassuring her, and after a couple of goes she really got the hang of it. The funny thing is, teaching her actually brought home how much I do on autopilot. When you've cooked something a hundred times, you stop thinking about it — but the moment you have to explain every step out loud, you realise there's a proper method behind it. So, in a way, breaking it down for her sharpened my own understanding, and I even picked up a few shortcuts along the way. As for whether informal learning matters as much as formal schooling — absolutely, I'd say it does. School gives you the theory, but the real practical stuff, the tricks of the trade, tends to be passed down from friends and family, often without you even noticing. At the end of the day, some of the most useful things I know I never learnt in a classroom — I learnt them hands-on, through trial and error.

bulletPoints: Describe a time you taught someone a practical skill.
How did teaching others help you refine your own understanding of that skill?
Why is informal education (learning from others) as important as formal schooling?
questions.sampleAnswer:
I once taught my younger cousin how to ride a bicycle. He was about eight years old at the time, and he was really eager to learn, but also quite nervous. I started by explaining the basics of balance and steering, and then I ran alongside him, holding onto the bike, until he got the feel of it. Gradually, I let go for short periods, encouraging him to keep pedaling and maintain his balance. It was a trial by fire, but he eventually got the hang of it.

Teaching him actually helped me refine my own understanding of balance and coordination. You don't really think about these things consciously when you've been riding a bike for years, but explaining them to someone else forces you to break down the process into its fundamental components. It made me appreciate the subtle adjustments and instinctive movements involved in maintaining balance. Furthermore, I understood the importance of patience and encouragement when passing on a skill.

Informal education, or learning from others, is absolutely as important as formal schooling. Formal schooling provides a structured curriculum and standardized knowledge, but informal education allows for personalized learning and the transmission of practical skills and tacit knowledge that aren't always taught in schools. Learning from family members, friends, or mentors can provide invaluable insights and perspectives that complement formal education. Experience is the best teacher, and informal education often provides that experience.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bir marta men kichik amakivachchamga velosiped haydashni o'rgatganman. O'shanda u sakkiz yoshlar atrofida edi va o'rganishga juda ishtiyoqi bor edi, lekin biroz xavotirda ham edi. Men unga muvozanat va rulni boshqarish asoslarini tushuntirishdan boshladim, keyin u velosipedni his qila boshlaguncha, velosipedni ushlab, uning yonida yugurdim. Asta-sekin, uni pedalni bosishda davom etishga va muvozanatini saqlashga undab, qisqa muddatlarga qo'yib yubordim. Bu oson bo'lmadi, lekin u oxir-oqibat uddaladi.

Unga o'rgatish, aslida, muvozanat va koordinatsiya haqidagi o'z tushunchamni yaxshilashga yordam berdi. Ko'p yillar davomida velosiped haydab yurganingizda, bu narsalar haqida ongli ravishda o'ylamaysiz, lekin ularni boshqa birovga tushuntirish jarayonni uning asosiy tarkibiy qismlariga ajratishga majbur qiladi. Bu menga muvozanatni saqlashda ishtirok etadigan nozik tuzatishlar va instinktiv harakatlarni qadrlashga yordam berdi. Bundan tashqari, men ko'nikmani o'rgatishda sabr-toqat va rag'batlantirishning muhimligini tushundim.

Norasmiy ta'lim, yoki boshqalardan o'rganish, rasmiy maktab ta'limi kabi juda muhimdir. Rasmiy maktab ta'limi tuzilgan o'quv dasturi va standartlashtirilgan bilimlarni taqdim etadi, lekin norasmiy ta'lim shaxsiy o'rganish va maktablarda har doim ham o'rgatilmaydigan amaliy ko'nikmalar va yashirin bilimlarni uzatish imkonini beradi. Oila a'zolari, do'stlar yoki ustozlardan o'rganish rasmiy ta'limni to'ldiradigan bebaho tushunchalar va nuqtai nazarlarni taqdim etishi mumkin. Tajriba eng yaxshi o'qituvchidir va norasmiy ta'lim ko'pincha shu tajribani taqdim etadi.

questions.prompt: Exams Should Be Held in All Schools
questions.sampleA1: Exams are good. They show what you know. Some students don't like exams.
questions.sampleA2: Exams are important, but they are stressful. Some students do well, and some do not. Exams can be unfair because some students are nervous.
questions.sampleB1: Exams help measure knowledge. They make students study hard. For example, they revise their notes. However, exams can be stressful. Some students get anxious. It is important to find a balance.
questions.sampleB2: Well, this is a real bone of contention, and I can see valid points on both sides, to be honest. On the one hand, those in favour argue that exams are the fairest way to measure what students actually know. They give everyone the same yardstick, and let's face it, the pressure does spur students on to knuckle down and revise. On top of that, exams prepare young people for the real world — university entrance, job interviews, deadlines — where you often have to perform under pressure whether you like it or not. On the other hand, the critics have a point too. Exams can pile on the stress, and for some students that anxiety gets in the way of showing what they're truly capable of. I mean, a bright student might completely freeze up on the day and end up with marks that don't reflect their ability at all. What's more, exams tend to reward memorising facts rather than creativity or critical thinking, which are arguably just as important in the long run. After all, the world doesn't hand out marks for regurgitating a textbook. So where do I stand? Personally, I'd sit somewhere in the middle. I don't think we should do away with exams altogether, because they clearly serve a purpose, but I do believe they shouldn't be the be-all and end-all. A fairer system would weigh up exams alongside coursework, projects and presentations, so you'd get a much rounder picture of what each student can genuinely do.

questions.sampleAnswer:
Undoubtedly, the debate surrounding exams in schools is complex, with valid arguments on both sides. Advocates for exams often highlight their role in measuring student knowledge and encouraging hard work. Exams provide a standardized way to assess what students have learned and motivate them to revise and keep up with the curriculum. Furthermore, they argue that exams prepare students for future challenges, such as university entrance exams and professional certifications. It builds resilience.

However, critics of exams point to the stress and anxiety they can cause. Exams can create an unhealthy level of pressure, leading to mental health issues and a fear of failure. Moreover, exams often fail to measure creativity, critical thinking, and other essential skills that are difficult to quantify. It's like trying to fit a square peg in a round hole. Finally, exams can be unfair due to factors such as test anxiety, cultural biases, and varying levels of preparation.

Ultimately, a balanced approach is needed. While exams can play a role in assessing student learning, they should not be the sole measure of success. Schools should also incorporate other forms of assessment, such as projects, presentations, and portfolios, to provide a more holistic evaluation of student abilities. All that glitters is not gold, and exam results don't always reflect true potential.

Shubhasiz, maktablardagi imtihonlar atrofidagi bahs murakkab bo'lib, har ikki tomonda ham asosli dalillar mavjud. Imtihonlarni yoqlab chiqadiganlar ko'pincha ularning o'quvchilar bilimini o'lchash va qattiq mehnat qilishga undashdagi rolini ta'kidlaydilar. Imtihonlar o'quvchilarning nimani o'rganganini baholashning standartlashtirilgan usulini taqdim etadi va ularni takrorlashga va o'quv dasturidan ortda qolmaslikka undaydi. Bundan tashqari, ular imtihonlar o'quvchilarni universitetga kirish imtihonlari va professional sertifikatlar kabi kelajakdagi qiyinchiliklarga tayyorlaydi, deb ta'kidlaydilar. Bu chidamlilikni shakllantiradi.

Biroq, imtihonlarni tanqid qiluvchilar ularning keltirib chiqarishi mumkin bo'lgan stress va xavotirga ishora qiladilar. Imtihonlar sog'lom bo'lmagan bosim darajasini yaratishi, ruhiy salomatlik muammolariga va muvaffaqiyatsizlikdan qo'rqishga olib kelishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, imtihonlar ko'pincha ijodkorlik, tanqidiy fikrlash va miqdoriy baholash qiyin bo'lgan boshqa muhim ko'nikmalarni o'lchay olmaydi. Bu dumaloq teshikka to'rtburchak mix tiqishga o'xshaydi. Nihoyat, imtihonlar test xavotiri, madaniy tarafkashlik va turli darajadagi tayyorgarlik kabi omillar tufayli adolatsiz bo'lishi mumkin.

Oxir oqibat, muvozanatli yondashuv zarur. Imtihonlar o'quvchilarning bilimini baholashda rol o'ynashi mumkin bo'lsa-da, ular muvaffaqiyatning yagona o'lchovi bo'lmasligi kerak. Maktablar, shuningdek, o'quvchilarning qobiliyatlarini yanada yaxlit baholashni ta'minlash uchun loyihalar, taqdimotlar va portfoliolar kabi baholashning boshqa shakllarini ham qo'shishi kerak. Yaltiroqning hammasi ham oltin emas va imtihon natijalari har doim ham haqiqiy salohiyatni aks ettirmaydi.
